senses.gloss: (b. h.; v. סָכַל I) to be bright.
to be wise, understand; to consider, deliberate.
units: <cite ref="Midrash Mishlei 1:3">Midr. Prov. to I, 3</cite> <he>כיון … צריך להַשְׂכִּיל היאך וכ׳</he> when a man is appointed judge, he must deliberate how to acquit the innocent &c.; <he>צריך להשכיל ולדקדק וכ׳</he> he must study and investigate the law, that he may not sin or lead to sin; Yalk. ib. 929 <he>צריך להשכיל היאך לדקדק וכ׳</he> he must deliberate how to carry out the law exactly &c.

<cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 32:1">Midr. Till. to Ps. XXXII</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="I Samuel 18:14">I Sam. XVIII, 14</cite>, sq.) <he>ומפני שהיה מַשְׂכִּיל היה כסוי חטאה</he> and because he was wise, his sin was covered; a. fr.

senses.gloss: to look towards, face; (cmp. סָכַם, a. כּוּן) to be directed.
units: <cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 14:21">Num. R. s. 14<sup>5</sup></cite>; <cite ref="Pesikta Rabbati 3:1">Pesik. R. s. 3</cite> (ref. to <he>שִׂכֵּל את ידיו</he>, <cite ref="Genesis 48:14">Gen. XLVIII, 14</cite>) <he>הִשְׂכִּילוּ ידיו … לרוח הקדש</he> Jacob’s hands were directed towards (pointed to) the holy spirit.
